questions.q: A patient with severe thrombocytopenia develops petechiae and mucosal bleeding, while PT and aPTT are normal. Which haemostatic process is most directly impaired?
options: Formation of the primary platelet plug
Conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin by thrombin
Activation of factor X by the tissue factor pathway
Cross-linking of fibrin by factor XIII
questions.explain: Platelets adhere to exposed subendothelial collagen via von Willebrand factor and platelet GPIb, then activate and aggregate to form the primary haemostatic plug. Thrombocytopenia therefore causes mucocutaneous bleeding; PT and aPTT can remain normal because they primarily assess plasma coagulation pathways.

questions.q: A patient taking low-dose aspirin has reduced platelet aggregation in response to arachidonic acid. Which platelet enzyme is irreversibly inhibited by aspirin?
questions.explain: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet cyclo-oxygenase-1 (COX-1), reducing thromboxane A2 synthesis and platelet activation/aggregation. Platelets cannot synthesise new COX-1, so the effect lasts for the platelet lifespan.

questions.q: A patient with severe vitamin K deficiency develops prolonged PT and aPTT. Which group of clotting factors is most directly affected by impaired gamma-carboxylation?
options: Factors II, VII, IX and X
Factors I, V, VIII and XIII
questions.explain: Vitamin K is required for gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX and X, as well as proteins C and S. This permits calcium-dependent binding to phospholipid surfaces.

questions.q: A patient has an isolated prolonged aPTT that corrects after mixing with normal plasma. What is the most likely interpretation?
questions.explain: Correction after mixing supports a factor deficiency because normal plasma supplies the missing factor. Failure to correct suggests an inhibitor.

questions.q: Which enzyme is primarily responsible for degrading fibrin within a formed blood clot?
questions.explain: Plasmin is generated from plasminogen, principally through tissue plasminogen activator. It digests fibrin and produces fibrin-degradation products.
